laws.name: Aesthetic-Usability Effect
laws.ask: Does it look cared for, and is that hiding a usability fault nobody has tested?

laws.name: Choice Overload
laws.ask: How many options are on the screen at once, and which could be defaults?

laws.name: Chunking
laws.ask: Is related information grouped into pieces a person can name?

laws.name: Cognitive Bias
laws.ask: Which bias is this design leaning on, and is that fair to the person?

laws.name: Cognitive Load
laws.ask: What does the person have to hold in mind to get through this?

laws.name: Doherty Threshold
laws.ask: Does anything between the action and its feedback take longer than four hundred milliseconds?

laws.name: Fitts's Law
laws.ask: Is every control pressable across its whole box, and is the box big enough to hit?

laws.name: Flow
laws.ask: Does anything interrupt the person mid-task that could have waited?

laws.name: Goal-Gradient Effect
laws.ask: Can the person see how close they are to done?

laws.name: Hick's Law
laws.ask: How many choices, of what complexity, sit in front of the person at once?

laws.name: Jakob's Law
laws.ask: Does this work the way the person's other tools already work?

laws.name: Law of Common Region
laws.ask: Does a boundary enclose exactly the things that belong together?

laws.name: Law of Prägnanz
laws.ask: Is the simplest reading of this screen the right one?

laws.name: Law of Proximity
laws.ask: Are things that belong together near each other, and things that do not, apart?

laws.name: Law of Similarity
laws.ask: Do things that look alike behave alike, and do things that differ look different?

laws.name: Law of Uniform Connectedness
laws.ask: Are connected things drawn as connected?

laws.name: Mental Model
laws.ask: Does the person's picture of how this works match how it works?

laws.name: Miller's Law
laws.ask: How many items does this ask the person to hold at once?

laws.name: Occam's Razor
laws.ask: What could be removed with nothing lost?

laws.name: Paradox of the Active User
laws.ask: Does it work for someone who will never read the instructions?

laws.name: Pareto Principle
laws.ask: Which few actions carry most of the use, and are they the easiest?

laws.name: Parkinson's Law
laws.ask: Does the flow give the task a natural end, or let it sprawl?

laws.name: Peak-End Rule
laws.ask: What is the peak moment and the last moment, and are they good?

laws.name: Postel's Law
laws.ask: Does it accept what people plausibly give and send only what they expect?

laws.name: Selective Attention
laws.ask: What will the person not see because they are looking for something else?

laws.name: Serial Position Effect
laws.ask: Is the important item first or last, never buried in the middle?

laws.name: Tesler's Law
laws.ask: Where does the complexity that cannot be removed live, and is it in one place?

laws.name: Von Restorff Effect
laws.ask: Does the one thing that must stand out actually differ from the rest?

laws.name: Working Memory
laws.ask: Does the person have to remember something from an earlier screen to finish this one?

laws.name: Zeigarnik Effect
laws.ask: Is unfinished work visibly unfinished?
